atoms.text:
Das Gerundium ist eine Form, bei der das Verb zu einem Nomen substantiviert wird. Es wird gebildet, indem man an den Infinitiv des Verbs die Endung -ing anhängt:

`Verbstamm +``ing`
atoms.sound: Das Gerundium ist eine Form, bei der das Verb zu einem Nomen substantiviert wird. Es wird gebildet, indem man an den Infinitiv des Verbs die Endung i n g anhängt.

atoms.text: Ob man das Gerundium oder den Infinitiv verwendet, hängt vom Kontext, bestimmten Verben und Satzkonstruktionen ab.

example.a: I love <m-yellow>having</m-yellow> nice conversations with friends.
example.sound: I love having nice conversations with friends.

example.a: They want <m-blue>to see</m-blue> my new bicycle.
example.sound: They want to see my new bicycle.

atoms.text: Das Gerundium wird verwendet, wenn auf Verben, Adjektive oder Nomen eine Präposition folgt.

example.a: This is the advantage of living in a house.
example.sound: This is the advantage of living in a house.

example.a: I believe in giving second chances.
example.sound: I believe in giving second chances.

example.a: He felt good about lending his sister money.
example.sound: He felt good about lending his sister money.

atoms.text: Das Gerundium wird auch nach bestimmten Verben verlangt, zum Beispiel nach to admit, to consider, to delay, to help, to finish und to practice.

example.a: He delayed telling his family about his detention.
example.sound: He delayed telling his family about his detention.

example.a: My family often considers selling the house.
example.sound: My family often considers selling the house.

atoms.text: Auch nach bestimmten Phrasen verwendet man das Gerundium:
atoms.sound: Auch nach bestimmten Phrasen verwendet man das Gerundium.

example.a: It's no use going after them.
example.sound: It's no use going after them.

example.a: I don't mind helping you once a week.
example.sound: I don't mind helping you once a week.

atoms.text: Nach Adjektiven und Nomen ohne Präposition folgt der Infinitiv.

example.a: She didn’t have time to call her friend.
example.sound: She didn’t have time to call her friend.

example.a: It felt amazing to watch the athletes in real life.
example.sound: It felt amazing to watch the athletes in real life.

atoms.text: Der Infinitiv wird außerdem nach bestimmten Verben verwendet, zum Beispiel nach to ask, to expect, to invite, to need, to want und to wish.
atoms.sound: Der Infinitiv wird außerdem nach bestimmten Verben verwendet, zum Beispiel nach: to ask, to expect, to invite, to need, to want und to wish.

example.a: We were asked to leave the premises.
example.sound: We were asked to leave the premises.

example.a: They invited me to stay for dinner.
example.sound: They invited me to stay for dinner.

atoms.text: Viele Verben können sowohl mit dem Gerundium als auch mit dem Infinitiv verwendet werden. Bei einigen Verben ändert sich dabei allerdings die Bedeutung:
atoms.sound: Viele Verben können sowohl mit dem Gerundium als auch mit dem Infinitiv verwendet werden. Bei einigen Verben ändert sich dabei allerdings die Bedeutung.

example.a: I forgot baking this cake would mean I had to clean up afterwards.
example.b: forgetting something that happened in the past
example.sound: I forgot baking this cake would mean I had to clean up afterwards.

example.a: Do not forget to do your homework.
example.sound: Do not forget to do your homework.

example.a: I remember locking the door.
example.b: remembering something that happened in the past
example.sound: I remember locking the door.

example.a: You must remember to buy lemons.
example.sound: You must remember to buy lemons.

example.a: I stopped listening to the teacher.
example.sound: I stopped listening to the teacher.

example.a: He stopped (doing something) to listen to the teacher more closely.
example.b: an action was stopped in order to do the described action
example.sound: He stopped to listen to the teacher more closely.

example.a: I can't go on working next to him.
example.sound: I can't go on working next to him.

example.a: After playing basketball, we go on to eat ice cream.
example.sound: After playing basketball, we go on to eat ice cream.

example.a: She will try playing chess.
example.sound: She will try playing chess.

example.a: They tried to find the keys.
example.b: to do something that isn’t easy
example.sound: They tried to find the keys.

example.a: To do all this homework means working on it all day long.
example.b: something that has to be done to get a result
example.sound: To do all this homework means working on it all day long.

example.a: I meant to give you the answers.
example.sound: I meant to give you the answers.

example.a: I regret asking him to come to my party.
example.b: something one did in the past and isn’t happy about
example.sound: I regret asking him to come to my party.

example.a: I regret to tell you, but the train was cancelled.
example.b: telling bad news one is not happy about
example.sound: I regret to tell you, but the train was cancelled.

example.a: She is used to getting up early.
example.b: the person is familiar with something
example.sound: She is used to getting up early.

example.a: He used to do crosswords in his free time.
example.b: the person did something in the past
example.sound: He used to do crosswords in his free time.
